title: CVE-2026-131868 - Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via a declared element length passed unchecked to sysread in asn_read and asn_get
summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-131868
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 1:17 a.m. | 41 minutes ago
Description :Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via a declared element length passed unchecked to sysread in asn_read and asn_get. The length an element declares in its BER header is passed to sysread as the read size. Perl grows the target buffer to that size before reading, so memory is allocated from the declared length, not from the data received. A 6-byte header can declare a length of up to 4GB. A single header makes the reading process allocate the declared size. Where the allocation fails, perl exits with "Out of memory", which eval cannot catch.

title: phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution
summary:
PHP's default file-based session storage can be made to return objects an attacker chose, by cutting off a session write at the right moment. When combined with a second weakness, such as a suitable gadget chain in the app, those objects can allow the attacker to run code on the server.

summary:
Impact

The query REST API allows executing HQL queries to filter the listed pages. While this properly checks access rights for the current user, the query can be used to combine when clauses and blind queries, to recover values, through FROM clause injection to join BaseObject and StringProperty tables, bypassing the HQL validator's SELECT column whitelist. This allows recovering any data that is stored in the database, including data from inaccessible pages, password hashes and passwords stored in configuration properties. For a typical password hash, this requires about 800 requests to the REST API (about one per bit).
